rejected.title: Strategies for inclusion
card: Strategies for inclusion are actions that help people take part in work, services, decisions and social life. Governments, schools, businesses and community groups can all use them.
Laws
Anti-discrimination laws make it unlawful to treat people unfairly on grounds such as disability, race, sex or age. A person treated unfairly can make a complaint.
Accessible services
Services are designed so more people can use them. Examples are ramps, interpreters and information in plain language.
Education and community programs
Education builds skills and knowledge that can open the way to work. Community programs, such as a local mentoring or language group, can link people with others and with support.
rejected.remember: Inclusion can be supported through law, accessible services, education and community programs.

a.q: A library adds a lift and Auslan interpreters at events so more locals can attend. Which strategy is this?
a.why: A lift and interpreters change the service itself so more people can use it. That is accessibility. It is not a law, because no rule is made about unfair treatment, and it is not a course or a group program.
a.clue: The change is to how the service itself is built and run.

b.q: A café refuses to serve Priya because she uses a wheelchair. Which strategy gives her a formal way to challenge this?
opts: A skills course at a local school
b.why: Anti-discrimination law makes this treatment unlawful and lets Priya make a complaint. A mentoring program may offer support and connection, but it does not give her a formal way to challenge the refusal.
b.clue: Which strategy sets a rule that can be enforced through a complaint?
